evidence_synthesis.approximate_weighted_central_tendency: Across 6 individual puskesmas/klinik pratama outpatient studies the error rate ranges 33-82%, with most clustering 45-73%. The systematic review of 10 puskesmas studies found accuracy 26-45% (error rate 55-74%).
evidence_synthesis.comparison_to_original_claim: The original 18% inaccuracy figure (from RSUD Pandan Arang inpatient, n=100) appears to substantially UNDERESTIMATE FKTP outpatient coding error rates. All identified FKTP-specific studies report error rates between 33% and 82%, with a median around 55-60%.
evidence_synthesis.direction_of_bias: The original claim likely creates downward bias in the PP1.2 cost model. A more conservative FKTP-appropriate estimate is 33-73% coding error rate (with 55% as a reasonable midpoint), not 18%.
evidence_synthesis.note_on_fktp_specificity: FKTP outpatient coding is done primarily by physicians, nurses, and midwives without formal medical records/coding training (unlike hospitals which have PMIK-certified coders). This structural difference explains why FKTP error rates are systematically higher than inpatient hospital error rates.
evidence_synthesis.bpjs_aggregate_data_gap: No BPJS Kesehatan aggregate FKTP claim rejection rate broken down by ICD-10 coding error specifically was found in DJSN quarterly reports — these reports track utilization and KBK performance but not coding accuracy metrics.

refined_claim: ICD-10 diagnosis coding error rates at Indonesian BPJS FKTP primary care facilities (puskesmas and klinik pratama) range from approximately 33% to 82% across multiple outpatient studies (n=77 to n=385 per study), with a weighted midpoint of approximately 55-60%. This is substantially higher than the 18% inpatient figure from RSUD Pandan Arang (Jan-Mar 2023, n=100) that was previously used as a proxy. A conservative FKTP-specific estimate for the PP1.2 cost model should use 33-73% (midpoint ~55%) rather than 18%.
original_claim_assessment: The original 18% figure is not wrong as a description of RSUD Pandan Arang inpatient performance, but it severely underestimates FKTP outpatient coding error rates, which multiple independent studies show are 2-4x higher. Using 18% as proxy for FKTP coding errors in the cost model would substantially understate both the problem prevalence and the value of a clinical AI coding-assist solution at FKTP level.
narrative_summary: Deep research confirms that ICD-10 coding error rates at Indonesian FKTP primary care facilities (puskesmas and klinik pratama) are substantially higher — not lower — than the 18% inpatient figure used in the original claim. A 2021 systematic review of 10 puskesmas studies (45 articles, 2009-2019) found puskesmas coding accuracy only 26-45%, implying a 55-74% error rate. Five additional individual puskesmas/klinik pratama outpatient studies published 2024-2026 corroborate this: error rates of 72.77% (Semarang puskesmas, n=98), 33.3% (Puskesmas Kijang, n=99, same Q1 2023 period), 54.8% (Puskesmas Gondokusuman, n=385), 45.83% (Puskesmas Ngampilan, n=95), and 58.44% (Puskesmas Baubau, n=77). One direct klinik pratama (BPJS FKTP klinik) study found an 82.14% error rate specifically for hypertension coding (n=84, Jan-Jun 2024). The structural reason is clear across all studies: FKTP coding is performed by clinicians (physicians, nurses, midwives) without PMIK certification or dedicated coding training, unlike hospitals. No BPJS aggregate FKTP claim rejection data broken down by coding error type was found in DJSN monitoring reports. The verdict is REFINED: the claim's direction is correct (coding errors are a real problem) but the magnitude is significantly underestimated; the PP1.2 cost model should substitute a FKTP-appropriate error rate of approximately 33-73% (central estimate ~55%) in place of the 18% inpatient proxy.
